- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply a 2–5 day lag correction, dampening forecast by 10–20% in the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤ -0.33) and price drops >3%, model frequently undercorrects; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for next 2–3 periods.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.33) and price is volatile, model tends to overfit short-term noise; use 10-day moving average as a smoothing anchor for next forecast.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3+ consecutive days, apply a “reversion bias” correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until price stabilizes.
